clue.text: Force subject to go ahead of time

parts.note: a theme is the subject of a talk or piece
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An order that something must happen early, as if a schedule were being forced forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go ahead of' simply places the subject before the time. The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A police service is called a force, and the Met is the familiar name of London's Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Chief's approach that shows where one is lying

definitions.text: that shows where one is lying
definitions.note: a relative clause describing the thing, standing in for the noun

parts.note: a head is a chief, with the possessive s
tone is the manner or approach someone takes

explanation.surface: A boss's manner reveals when someone is telling untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests telling fibs, but here it is lying buried in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone marks the spot where a person lies buried.

clue.text: It catches fellow removing parking slogan

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: removing means taking something away, here the letter for parking

parts.note: a trap is something that catches
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A traffic warden nabs someone and takes away their parking motto.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the trap first, but the fellow comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a phrase repeated constantly, a watchword or slogan.

clue.text: Be straight and count on rising position

parts.note: to tell is an old word for count, as a bank teller does

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: Be honest and rely on your status improving.
explanation.definitionFit: To be straight with someone is to be honest, never telling them a falsehood.

clue.text: Somewhat dejected from constant involvement in wild dancing

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to mosh is to dance wildly at a rock or punk gig
pi is the best-known mathematical constant

explanation.surface: Someone feels a bit low after being swept up in frenzied dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopish means given to moping, gloomy and listless, which is a mild form of dejection.

clue.text: Major episode demands intensive care — initially from her?

definitions.text: Major episode demands intensive care — initially from her?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A serious medical crisis needs intensive care, which is supplied by a health worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: in a serious incident needing intensive care, she is the one who provides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is a doctor or medical worker, the person who gives such care.

clue.text: Joke attempt to trap detective giving expert opinion

indicators.note: trapping something means holding it inside, so the other pieces surround it

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
DI is a Detective Inspector
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag is aimed at catching out a sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: Punditry is the commentary of pundits, people paid for their expert views.

clue.text: Basic trail switches left to right

indicators.note: switching from one to the other means one letter is swapped out for a different one

parts.note: to stalk someone is to trail them
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A simple footpath that zigzags from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means bare and plain, stripped down to the essentials.

clue.text: Approach station guide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a route or means of approach
second meaning: a broadcasting station, and also to guide or direct something along a course

explanation.surface: Reads like the way into a railway station, or a guidebook to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station guide' can be read as two further meanings: a TV station, and the verb to guide water or energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers a route of access and a broadcasting frequency, and the verb means to direct something along a course.

clue.text: Unite worried following argument against firm

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the worried piece is placed second, behind the argument and the firm

parts.note: pros and cons: the con is the argument against
solid means firm
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: Bring together staff who are anxious after a dispute with their company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the worried piece after the other two; 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate is to combine several things into a single stronger whole.

clue.text: Study target country

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
a mark is something aimed at

explanation.surface: A researcher choosing which nation to focus their work on.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: It's a lot of money for customised snoring mask

indicators.note: customised means altered to suit, so the letters are remade in a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Complaining about the steep price of a bespoke anti-snoring device.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a huge sum, originally what would be paid to free a captured monarch.

clue.text: Elderly are proceeding cautiously about publicity, being nervous

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: nosing along means edging forward carefully
PR is public relations, or publicity
to be chicken is to be scared

explanation.surface: Old people moving warily around the media spotlight because they feel jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is no spring chicken is an idiom for saying they are no longer young.

clue.text: Instrument that hurt lover, so they say

indicators.note: so they say points to what people utter, so the clue words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: OW is a cry when hurt and a beau is a lover; said together they match the instrument's name

explanation.surface: Gossip about a musical instrument that caused a sweetheart pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A beau is a boyfriend; 'Ow, beau!' is how the sound is reached.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: They help calculate some playground regulations?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sliding scaled rulers used for arithmetic before calculators
second meaning, whimsical: rules for using the slides in a playground

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a playful reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: These logarithmic rulers were the engineer's calculating tool, and the words can also be read as rules for slides.

clue.text: Knock down deals for ocean travellers

parts.note: to deck someone is to floor them with a punch
in cards, each deal gives a player a hand

explanation.surface: Bargain cruise offers being slashed in price.
explanation.definitionFit: Deckhands are crew members working on a ship's deck, so they travel the seas.

clue.text: Letters set down on ground

parts.note: to land is to set down, as an aircraft does
Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London

explanation.surface: Correspondence dropped on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like post, but it means people who let property.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords let houses and rooms to tenants, so they are literally those who let.

clue.text: Surprising find in approachable energy supplier

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a warm person is friendly and approachable

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly friendly power company.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating electricity, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: Touring Venice, Enid gets present

indicators.note: touring suggests moving around, so the letters travel into a new order

parts.note: the two names taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tourist called Enid receives a gift while going round Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in evidence is plainly visible and on hand, which is what being present means.

clue.text: Old Americans needing some skincare

definitions.note: plural; the answer can serve as a plural for the people

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next word

parts.note: the letters straddle the join of skin and care

explanation.surface: Ancient peoples requiring a bit of moisturiser.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the pre-Columbian rulers of an empire in the Andes, so they are old Americans.

clue.text: Staggered and troubled when overheard

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: fazed means disconcerted or troubled

explanation.surface: Someone reeled and was upset when they caught what was being said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' suggests reeling, but means spread out in stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Phased work is carried out in stages, so its start times are staggered.

clue.text: Rampant ill health's so sad at this great age

indicators.note: rampant means running wild and unchecked, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A lament that widespread sickness is miserable for someone so old.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extremely old, which matches being of a very great age.

clue.text: Performing dance that's easy to get?

parts.note: an actor who is on is performing
tap is a style of dance

explanation.surface: A routine on stage that is simple to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is readily available whenever wanted, like beer from a barrel.

clue.text: Determined to have some music that's uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: music is made of notes

explanation.surface: Resolved to own a few cheerful tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means having firmly resolved to do it.

clue.text: Take out more? Cashpoint is empty

parts.note: extra means additional, more

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, so only its outside letters survive

parts.note: just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants to withdraw more money but the cash machine has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: A cashpoint is a British cash machine or ATM.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to remove or pull it out.

clue.text: Ignore hipster's essentially strange solution for everything

parts.note: to ignore a request is in effect to answer no

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Dismiss a trendy person's weird remedy that claims to cure all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, meaning peculiar, is a common old-fashioned British word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet scheme claimed to cure every ill, a supposed panacea.

clue.text: Call father back to meet a distant relation

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from the end towards the start

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Phone your dad again to arrange to see a far-off cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Early humanlike primates are evolutionary ancestors, so an ape-man is a very remote relative of ours.

clue.text: Cruel type displays a disturbing piece

indicators.note: a piece is only a part, so the answer is a stretch of the words before it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across into the third

explanation.surface: A cruel person shows off an upsetting work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain, the very model of a cruel person.
